title: Memory uncertainty weakens a stationary-model test of the 2007-2025 CalCOFI oxygen low on sigma0 26.5
abstract: We tested whether low oxygen after 2006 requires a new state. We used a published CalCOFI annual index on sigma0 26.5. A stationary Gaussian model fitted to 47 values in 1950-2006 had a 5-year memory. Given the low in 2006, the lower-tail probability of the 2007-2025 mean was 0.00664 with parameters held fixed. In 10,000 simulations that repeat model fitting, the conditional test gave p = 0.0541. A 20-year memory was not excluded by an earlier-record simulation test (p = 0.221). With that memory and fitted mean and variance, the later low had conditional probability about 0.308. Thus the rare observed level does not by itself establish a permanent state. The fixed-effects index and sigma0 26.7 gave stronger evidence against their fitted stationary models. Results depend on the index, Gaussian model, year gaps and retrospective split. The bootstrap uses the fitted null and is not uniformly valid over all parameters. No physical cause or recovery time is identified. Code, model profiles, simulation results, a figure, provenance and a matrix audit are included; external source records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Ocean-memory uncertainty changes the test of persistent low oxygen. Data from CalCOFI; annual index from the cited SCI publication. See the main text for intervals and limits.
